sections.title: Theme presets
paragraphs: Applying a preset sets both colors, corner radius, pill behavior, and surface tone together. Individual controls can then be changed.

sections.title: Interface scale overrides
paragraphs: Top bar, Sidebar, Properties, Canvas controls, and Timeline can each use the global scale or override it with 50%, 75%, 100%, or 125%. Use global is represented by an empty override, so changing the global scale continues to affect that region.

sections.title: Shortcut defaults
paragraphs: Global shortcut conflicts are compared without case sensitivity. A duplicate global shortcut is rejected.

notice.title: Editor shortcut
notice.text: The preferences schema also contains the editor Play/Pause shortcut, Space, but the Recorder shortcut subview does not display it.

rows: View the application version, copy system information, open the changelog, and restart the Welcome Tour.

sections.title: Stored preference data
paragraphs: The normalized preference schema is version 3. In addition to visible controls, it stores onboarding completion, selected devices, saved background color and gradient presets, and whether the interaction notice was dismissed.

sections.title: Names, folders, and sessions
paragraphs: New recordings receive generated names such as Clever Comet or Rapid Signal. A numeric suffix is added when a generated name already exists. A project is a folder that can contain multiple recording sessions and their separate media tracks.

sections.title: Preview and badges
paragraphs: Beam prefers the persisted `thumbnail.webp`. If it is missing, Beam can generate a WebP thumbnail from the available preview source. Hovering a project plays its screen recording muted, automatically, and in a loop; scrolling cancels the hover preview and stops playback.

The project contains captions or a text layer.

notice.title: Badge scope
notice.text: The current Project Manager does not show separate microphone or system-audio badges.

sections.title: Batch deletion
paragraphs: A single-project delete asks for confirmation. Batch deletion starts directly from selection mode and deletes projects sequentially rather than starting every filesystem operation at once.

pages.title: Permissions and privacy
pages.description: Platform requirements and privacy behavior for screen, audio, camera, and interaction capture.
pages.lead: Beam requests protected capabilities only through the operating-system paths needed by the selected sources. Interaction recording is optional and does not store typed text.

sections.title: Windows
bullets: Screen and window capture use Windows Graphics Capture.
Cursor and click capabilities depend on what the Windows capture path exposes.
Interaction access does not require the Linux Polkit helper.

rows: macOS 13 or later; `NSAudioCaptureUsageDescription` is required from macOS 14.2.

sections.title: Linux

rows: XDG Desktop Portal v2 or later
Displays the system source picker and obtains recording consent.

Provides optional keyboard-shortcut and mouse-click metadata.
May be required to authorize and operate the input helper.
One screen or window is selected for the session; region capture is unavailable.

paragraphs: Keyboard shortcuts and mouse clicks can have different availability depending on accessible input devices. Linux interaction capture always reports that typed text is not recorded.

notice.title: Beam windows in full-screen capture
notice.text: Beam cannot hide its own windows from a Linux full-screen capture. Screen mode is still recommended; arrange Beam before confirming the portal selection.

sections.title: Interaction privacy
bullets: It runs only while a recording session is active.
It stores supported click metadata and safe shortcut tokens.
It never stores the text typed by the user.

sections.title: Media isolation and failure boundaries
paragraphs: Camera, microphone, and system audio are stored as separate tracks or sidecars where supported. Outside Linux, system audio uses Chromium display-media capture. Electron grants media access only to trusted application renderers. A camera reported unavailable during preparation can be omitted while capture continues; other camera or sidecar errors, and failure of a selected microphone or system-audio source, can stop recording startup.
